sentences.text:
The brief facts of the plaintiff's case are that:
a) That, the defendant Nos.5 and 6 are the absolute owners of the agricultural land and they have formed the revenue layout and they had sold the sites to various persons by executing the documents.

The plaintiff is one of the purchaser of site House List bearing No.3 of V.P.Katha No.20/3 measuring east to west 35 feet, north to south 52 feet situated at Vaddarapalya Village, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk i.e., suit schedule property.
The defendant Nos.5 and 6 had executed a registered sale deed dated 07.05.1996 in favour of the plaintiff in respect of the suit schedule property.

On placing of the registered sale deed dated 07.05.1996, the plaintiff got it assessment from the Secretary, Kothanuru Grama Panchayath and the tax has been fixed and the same been paid to the concerned authorities.
Since then the plaintiff is in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property.
The plaintiff has also put up the compound wall around the suit schedule property and protected from the trespassers.
Till today, the plaintiff is in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property without any interference.

The defendant Nos.5 and 6 being the land owners, who had formed the layout due to lost the agricultural characteristics, because it is situated near Vaddarapalya Village and all sites which are formed and identified by the Kothanur Grama Panchayath and assessment has been made in and around of the layout, which are fully devel oped.

The 1st defendant issued a notification acquiring the land for the purpose of formation of BDA layout, for which, the defendant Nos.5 and 6 filed detailed objection as they have sold the sites to the public, hence, it is not fit land for acquisition.
The said objection considered by the defendant Nos.1 to 4 and recognised the development made by the purchasers.

2b) It is further stated that, the adjacent owners were approached before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and sought for regularisation, which was considered by the defendant Nos.1 to 4 authorities.
The defendant No.3 authority unable to send the papers to the 4th defendant as unable to form the layout due to entire area was developed.
Hence, no layout has been formed and confirmed about possession of the plaintiff and others.
Even the 2 nd defendant has not taken any action to form the layout by directing the defendant Nos.3 and 4.
Since the defendant Nos.2 to 4 authorities unable to form the layout and made correspondence with 1st defendant for deletion.

The acquisition proceedings claimed by the defendant Nos.1 to 4 and the suit schedule property was carved from the agricultural land of Kothanuru Dinne were questioned the preliminary and final notification for formation of BTM layout before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and quashed the said notification and the said matter was reported in ILR 2011 KAR page 3657 in Sri Adikeshavalu Naidu Vs State of Karnataka and others.

It is surprise that, the defendant Nos.2 to 4 came near the suit schedule property during the last month of 26.02.2016 and tried to demolish the structure with their employees.

On these grounds, the 2 nd defendant prays to dismiss the suit.

3. Whether plaintiff is entitled for the relief as sought for ?

I have gone through the entire materials on record.

Issue Nos.1 to 3 :- In the affirmative, Issue No.4 :- As per final order;

sentences.text: As discussed above, the defendants though they have filed the written statement, but they have not produced any documents to show that, they have legally taken the possession by way of acquisition.
In the absence of material documents, it cannot be said that, the plaintiff is out of possession.
14. No doubt, the initial burden is on the plaintiff to prove that, he is in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property and the defendants are causing interference.
When the plaintiff has produced material documents before this Court to show that, he is in possession of the suit schedule property, the next burden shifts on the defendants to disprove the same.

At this stage, I would like to refer the citation reported in AIR 1999 SC page 1441 in the case of Vidhyadhar Vs Mankikrao and another, wherein, it is held that:
(A) Evidence Act (1 of 1872), S.114 - Adverse inference - Party to suit - Not entering the witness box - Give rise to inference adverse against him.

Where a party to the suit does not appear into the witness box and states his own case on oath and odes not offer himself to be cross examined by the other side, a presumption would arise that the case set up by him is not correct."
Thus, The facts and circumstances discussed in the above respected judgment and the facts and circumstances of the present case are one and the same.

Therefore, the principles laid down in the above respected judgment is aptly applicable to the case on hand, since the defendant No.2 who filed the written statement has not stepped into the witness box, and not offered for the cross-examination.
Under the said circumstances, as observed in the said ruling, the case putforth by the defendant No.2 is false.

15. Further, the learned counsel for the plaintiff has relied upon the rulings reported in:
 AIR 1997 Kerala 165 in the case of Ishwara Bhat Vs Annappa Naika.

The cause of action arose on 26.02.2016 and subsequently on 18.03.2016 when the defendant Nos.2 to 4 were interfered and the defendant Nos.5 and 6 were trying to interfere to take possession of the suit schedule property without authority of law.
The plaintiff has filed this suit with dishonest intention at the cause wrongful loss to this defendant.
The plaintiff is in knowledge of this defendant's acquisition and awarding compensation proceedings at time to time over the suit schedule property and by suppressing the real facts, he has filed this suit and hence, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
The plaintiff has suppressed the material facts before this Court and filed a false, frivolous suit.
At no point of time,
the defendant Nos.5 and 6 formed the revenue layout and they had sold the sites to various persons by executing the documents.
The 1 st defendant issued a notification acquiring the land for the purpose of formation of BDA layout, for which, the defendant Nos.5 and 6 filed detailed objection as they had sold the sites to the public, hence, it is not fit land for acquisition.
The said objection was considered by the defendant Nos.1 to 4 and recognised the development made by the purchasers.
The defendant No.3 authority unable to send the papers to the 4th defendant as unable to form the layout due to entire area was developed.
Hence, no layout has been formed and confirmed about his possession and others.
Even the 2 nd defendant has not taken any action to form the layout by directing the defendant No.3 and since the defendant Nos.2 to 4 authorities unable to form the layout and made correspondence with 1st defendant for deletion.
The acquisition proceedings claimed by the defendant Nos.1 to 4 and the suit schedule property was carved from the agricultural land of Kothanuru Dinne were questioned the preliminary and final notification for formation of BTM layout before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and quashed the said notification and the said matter was reported in ILR 2011 KAR page 3657 in Sri Adikeshavalu Naidu Vs State of Karnataka and others.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
By virtue of the registered sale deed executed by the defendant Nos.5 and 6, he is in peaceful and enjoyment of the suit schedule property.
To accept the contention of the defendant No.2, they have not produced any documentary evidence before this Court to show that,
the defendant Nos.1 to 4 had acquired the land in question and formed the sites and allotted to the beneficiaries and they have constructed the buildings in the land in question, nothing is putforth by the defendants.
Further, in the instant case, the sale deed obtained by the plaintiff and the katha accepted in his name have not been challenged by the defendants.
Till it is cancelled by the competent Court of law, it is having presumptive value.
In the absence of material documents, it cannot be said that, the plaintiff is out of possession.
Under the said circumstances, as observed in the said ruling, the case putforth by the defendant No.2 is false.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Accordingly, I answer issue Nos.1 to 3 are in the affirmative.
In view of my aforesaid discussions, I proceed to pass the following: -
ORDER
The suit of the plaintiff is hereby decreed with cost.
Permanent injunction is granted restraining the defendant Nos.1 to 4, their servants,
henchmen, supporters, agents and others acting under them from interfering with the plaintiffs peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property in any manner.
